topic: Everyday brain illusions: stopped clock, blind spot, doorway effect, phantom vibration, frequency illusion
hook: 5 ways your brain lies to you daily

slides.title: The frozen clock
slides.body: Glance at a clock and the first second feels longer. Your brain fills in the gap from your eye movement.
slides.image_prompt: Close-up of a vintage analog wall clock with its second hand mid-tick, soft dramatic light, slightly blurred motion trail

slides.title: Your hidden blind spot
slides.body: Each eye has a spot with no light sensors, where the optic nerve exits. Your brain quietly paints over it.
slides.image_prompt: Glass model of an eyeball on a dark surface with a small glowing hole at the back, moody scientific lighting

slides.title: The doorway effect
slides.body: Walking through a door can make you forget why you came. Studies suggest your brain files it as a new scene.
slides.image_prompt: Half-open wooden door in a dim hallway with bright light spilling through, floating faded sticky notes drifting away

slides.title: Phantom vibrations
slides.body: In one study, 89% of students felt their phone buzz when it hadn't. Your brain is primed to expect it.
slides.image_prompt: Smartphone lying face down on a wooden table with faint ghostly vibration lines around it, blank dark screen

slides.title: Suddenly everywhere
slides.body: Learn a new word and you see it all the time. It was always there. Your brain just started noticing.
slides.image_prompt: Magnifying glass over a crowded parking lot of grey cars where one red car glows sharply in focus

cta: Follow so you never miss the next one
caption:
Your brain doesn't show you reality. It shows you its best guess. Right now there is a hole in your vision, and you can't see it, because your brain fills it in.

These five glitches happen to almost everyone, every day. Researchers have studied each of them, from the 'stopped clock' illusion to phantom phone buzzes.

Which one happens to you the most? 👇
